card.title: New Rule Required
card.instruction: Use every problem as justification for adding another rule, ceremony, checkpoint, or layer of oversight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You spilled one cup. From now on, drinks need pouring permits.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if the supervisor spills one?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. I'll add an appeals procedure before we serve anything.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 converts a spill to permits; A3 adds a supervisor and A5 adds appeals, matching proliferating oversight.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 asks permit issuer and A3 names supervision, but A5 appeals does not clearly answer B4 supervisor spilling.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 reasonably test how the proposed system handles authority and its mistakes.

heightening.evidence: A5 blocks service with another process, but the particular appeal procedure lacks a stated connection to B4.

specificity.evidence: A1 spilled drink and B2 permits establish an overregulated pouring task.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 bureaucratic delay follows the style of A1, yet an appeals procedure reads as interchangeable jargon.

coach2.missing: B4-A5 lacks the essential link between a supervisor spilling and an appeal rather than cleanup or supervision.
coach2.firstDefect: First material weakness is B4-A5: the added procedure is not concretely caused by this problem.
